content: Emtricitabine and tenofovir have been detected in human breast milk. Regarding their use during pregnancy, they are generally considered acceptable, as controlled studies in pregnant women have not demonstrated any evidence of fetal risk. Emtricitabine is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI). After undergoing phosphorylation, it interferes with HIV viral DNA polymerase activity, thereby inhibiting viral replication. It is a cytosine analogue. Tenofovir is also a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI). Following hydrolysis and phosphorylation, it inhibits HIV-1 reverse transcriptase by competing with AMP as a substrate. These medications can be taken with or without food. Tablets should be swallowed whole and should not be chewed, crushed, broken, or dissolved. When comparing formulary status with other drugs in the same class, it is helpful to create a list of plans. This list can be saved and edited at any time. Adding plans allows for a comparison of formulary information, which may vary between individual plans. It is important to note that formulary information is subject to change, and for the most accurate and up-to-date details, you should contact the relevant plan provider.
